items_missed: No 'How are you today?' — went straight from greeting into the estimate ask
No agenda statement with a time estimate — 'Is now a good time for that?' is a permission ask, not 'I'll gather details then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes'

Never probed additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony), special considerations (long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns), storage stops, additional stops, or access concerns (parking, HOA) — notable given a three-story load-up
Never asked the moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Never stated the actual hourly rate per mover per hour — only quoted lump-sum totals ($2,688 / $2,304 / $2,016 / $1,728), so the customer can't sanity-check the math
Partial 'what's included' — covered blankets, stretch wrap, floor/door/wall protection, but skipped gas, truck, taxes, tools
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees)
Never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no 'prep shortens the move and lowers the bill', no consolidation examples, no carload tip
No booking attempt — routed to a virtual walkthrough without asking to hold the Sunday 8/23 slot he'd just confirmed was open
Didn't mention the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email or ask the customer to reply with corrections
Never gave office hours or a direct phone number — only 'my name will be at the bottom of the email'
No 60c/lb baseline alongside the $2,000 No Worries coverage
Used the customer's name only twice ('Is this Tim?' / 'Hey Tim')
top_strength: Excellent resource-right-sizing and transparency on the estimate — he opened with the full 4-movers/2-trucks number, then talked himself down to 3 movers on 1 truck for a partial move and gave the customer four concrete price points, explicitly accounting for the three-story load-up against the one-story unload.
coaching_note: He had a confirmed open Sunday and a warm, ready-to-move customer and never asked for the booking — route to the walkthrough AND hold the date in the same breath. Second priority: he quotes lump sums without ever saying the hourly rate per mover, which hides how the number is built.
phone_presence_notes: Consultative and genuinely helpful — proactively lowered the customer's price and offered himself as the walkthrough contact, and the customer closed with repeated unprompted thanks, though the delivery rambles in places.
